To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is significant variation in learning performance among colonies of the same species; (2) colonies with better learning performance are more successful foragers under natural conditions; and (3) this correlation is unlikely to be confounded by other factors
(i) learning speed varies among bumble-bees, (ii) learning speed correlates with natural foraging success and (iii) the correlation is steep, suggesting strong selection for higher speed

(i) learning speed of bumble-bee (Bombus terrestri) colonies is correlated to their foraging success in the field, (ii) this relationship holds even when the effect of other factors is taken into account, and (iii) this correlation suggests that learning speed may be an important factor in natural selection.
